related_questions.question: What is the #1 cause of depression?
related_questions.snippet: There's no single cause of depression. It can occur for a variety of reasons and it has many different triggers. For some people, an upsetting or stressful life event, such as bereavement, divorce, illness, redundancy and job or money worries, can be the cause. Different causes can often combine to trigger depression.

text_blocks.snippet: Depression is a common mental disorder affecting millions worldwide. In the US, an estimated 21 million adults experience at least one major depressive episode annually, representing 8.3% of the adult population. Women are more likely to be affected than men, with 10.3% of women experiencing a major depressive episode compared to 6.2% of men. Depression can significantly impact daily life, affecting work, home, and social activities.
snippet_highlighted_words: In the US, an estimated 21 million adults experience at least one major depressive episode annually, representing 8.3% of the adult population

list.snippet: Overall Prevalence: Around 8.3% of US adults experience a major depressive episode each year.
Age: Depression is most prevalent among young adults (18-25 years).
Gender: Women are more likely to be affected than men.
Race and Ethnicity: Prevalence varies across racial and ethnic groups, with higher rates among non-Hispanic White adults compared to other groups, according to the CDC.
Socioeconomic Status: Depression is also linked to lower socioeconomic status, with higher rates among those with less education and lower income.

list.title: Functional Impairment:
list.snippet: A large percentage of adults with depression report difficulty with work, home, and social activities.

list.title: Comorbidity:
list.snippet: Depression often co-occurs with other mental health conditions, such as anxiety disorders, and substance use disorders.

list.title: Physical Health:
list.snippet: People with depression are at higher risk for developing certain physical health problems, including cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.

list.title: Suicide:
list.snippet: Depression is a leading cause of suicide, highlighting the severity of the condition.

list.title: Treatment Rates:
list.snippet: A significant portion of individuals with depression do not receive treatment, with almost half of adults with major depressive disorder not accessing treatment.

list.title: Types of Treatment:
list.snippet: Effective treatments for depression include therapy (such as cognitive behavioral therapy) and medication.

list.title: Importance of Seeking Help:
list.snippet: Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for managing depression and improving outcomes.
The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that about 5% of adults worldwide suffer from depression.
Depression is more common in women than men, and it can affect people of all ages and backgrounds.
